The South Australian premier, Peter Malinauskas, says there is optimism that steel making will continue in his state, after the closure of a major blast furnace at Whyalla was announced yesterday.

Speaking to ABC News Breakfast from Whyalla and donned in some hi-vis, Malinauskas says there was disappointment, heartbreak, but also a sense of inevitability when the announcement was made.

[Whyalla] has the capacity to be a viable operation but it hasn’t been recapitalised. The blast furnace is over 60 years old. It was first built in 1965 and blast furnaces of this age not to be realigned on a frequent basis. This hasn’t been done in 20 years. The fact it’s still going is a miracle. We need to have the plant recapitalised and that’s exactly the plan we have in conjunction with the federal government … if we lose this capacity behind me, this country doesn’t have structural steel-making capacity and we can’t afford that.

There’s also retained optimism about the future of steel making in this country through that package, that $1.9bn package on the table as part of the sale process, which is why we’ve got to focus on the big picture here and the long term and make sure we account for the real impacts of yesterday’s decision.

If Pauline Hanson wants to take us down the road of Americanising our politics, so people in a family who disagree on political issues can’t speak to each other any longer, like, this is the pathway to do it …

We’ve got lots of challenges facing Australia, but we’re not going to solve them by punching down on things that are brilliant about our country. So I think it’s rotten. I think it’s awful. I think it’s ugly.

I just don’t agree with those comments. But I actually do agree with Senator Jacinta Nampijinpa Price when she says that there are serious issues that do need to be discussed. And these comments shouldn’t be a distraction from them. I mean, why aren’t we closing the gap?

Mark Rutte says attack that narrowly missed Boris Johnson and David Petraeus shows Vladimir Putin’s desperation

The head of Nato has said a Russian drone attack on a train close to Ukraine’s border with Poland would not deter Kyiv’s western backers.

Mark Rutte said the strike on a passenger train showed how desperate Vladimir Putin had become. “He thinks that he can stops us from supporting Ukraine and that he can undermine our unity. He is wrong. Our answer is to increase support,” the Nato general secretary said.

events.title: Sweden’s political parties launch coalition talks as both blocs try to secure power
events.summary:
Centre-left bloc led by Social Democrats has narrow lead with 95% of vote counted, but faces internal policy battle

Sweden’s political parties have launched coalition negotiations as the Social Democrats leader, Magdalena Andersson, started the long and difficult process of trying to form a new government.

Full results from Sunday’s election are not expected until after overseas votes are counted on Wednesday, but with 95% of the votes counted, the Social Democrats and the centre-left bloc had a narrow but growing lead of 176 seats to the right-leaning parties’ 173.

events.summary:
Soaring oil prices of above $108 a barrel after Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure stoke inflation fears

US government borrowing costs have risen to 5% for the first time since 2023 as soaring oil prices fuelled by the war in the Middle East trigger an intensifying sell-off in the global bond market.

The yield – in effect the interest rate – on 10-year US Treasury bonds hit the psychologically important threshold on Monday, on a day of renewed selling pressure on Wall Street as the global oil price reached $108 a barrel.

events.title: Trump says he will consider releasing more 9/11 records after families’ request
events.summary:
Families have asked Trump to declassify records that could shed light on Saudi Arabia’s alleged role in the 2001 attacks

Donald Trump said on Sunday that he will look into requests from families of 9/11 victims to release records that could shed light on Saudi Arabia’s alleged role in the attacks 25 years ago.

Several families have long alleged that a group of extremist religious leaders in Saudi Arabia gained influence in the kingdom’s government and aided the hijackers. Fifteen of the 19 hijackers were Saudis, but the Saudi government has long denied any involvement in the attacks.

Miki Zohar accuses Oscar-winning directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor of ‘treason against the state’

  • ‘They know the house they are bombing is full of children’: NAZA’s directors on their devastating film about Israeli intelligence

Israel’s culture minister has called for the Oscar-winning Israeli directors of NAZA, a documentary about the country’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, to be stripped of their citizenship, accusing them of “treason against the state”.

NAZA, which was produced by the Guardian, is named for an acronym used by Israel’s intelligence service to indicate how many civilians it expects to die in an airstrike on Gaza.

events.title: US airman recounts Iran rescue in 60 Minutes segment branded propaganda
events.summary:
Critics say segment about airman’s rescue was made to boost public perception of Trump’s unpopular war

A US airman has spoken of climbing a 7,000ft ridge with a broken back, arm and shoulder after he was shot down in Iran – and of being rescued by a team of American special forces as hostile locals closed in on him.

The air force colonel, identified only by his codename Bravo, appeared on camera Sunday night on CBS’s 60 Minutes in a segment some critics have labelled Pentagon propaganda to boost public perception of Donald Trump’s unpopular war.

events.title: Gulf states postpone strait of Hormuz talks with Iran as Yemen conflict intensifies
events.summary:
Impasse comes amid growing Saudi anger with Tehran over Houthi advances and strikes on airbase and pipeline

  • Oil prices rise after drone attacks shut down Saudi Arabia’s east-west pipeline

Gulf states have postponed a critical meeting with Iran on the future of the strait of Hormuz owing to a lack of Arab consensus and growing Saudi Arabian anger with Tehran for helping the Houthis loosen Riyadh’s grip in Yemen.

The stalemate over the vital waterway came as Houthi rebels launched a fresh barrage of missile and drone attacks on Saudi military targets. A Houthi military spokesperson claimed its forces had attacked the King Khalid airbase in Khamis Mushait, hitting fighter-jet hangars, radar systems, runways and landing strips, ammunition depots and additional targets.

events.title: CIA releases dozens of presidential daily briefs on Bin Laden and al-Qaida from before 9/11
events.summary:
The presidential briefing documents were declassified on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks

Several dozen presidential briefing documents declassified on Friday, the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, detail intelligence that government officials had gathered about Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida leading up to the hijackings that killed nearly 3,000 people and upended American national security.

The documents illustrate security analysts’ tracking of Bin Laden’s movements and support system, as well as concerns about possible threats to US targets. They also detail officials’ understanding of his network in the United States and other countries, including how his operations were financed.

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘Our forefathers are coming back’: Naga people celebrate after Oxford museum agrees to return remains
events.summary:
Following six years of talks, Pitt Rivers Museum will return body parts collected by British colonial administrators to north-east India

Anthropologists and community leaders from Nagaland, a remote state in north-eastern India bordering Myanmar, have expressed joy and relief that human remains belonging to their ancestors that had been on display in a British museum for nearly a century are finally being returned.

On Monday, the Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford announced that 39 pieces of human remains – including parts of skulls, a finger and a piece of skin with hair – belonging to the Naga tribes, will be returned to Nagaland after six years of negotiation between the community and the museum.

There isn’t much that we Indians agree on these days. GDP numbers are no exception. Last week, India released glowing GDP numbers for the latest quarter – 7.8% growth – higher than the forecast 7%. It sparked a furore.

Subhash Garg, a former finance secretary under Narendra Modi’s government and now a critic, reframed what Modi called a “herculean feat” as mere smoke and mirrors. According to Garg, the government revised last year’s current-price GDP downwards to inflate this year’s number – he believes the real growth is only 2.6%.

events.title: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster
events.summary:
Foreign minister Shisir Khanal tells the Guardian the world’s biggest economies need to help Nepal, which contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions

Nepal is demanding $20m in climate compensation for the recent devastating floods, as a senior minister called on the world’s most polluting countries to “wake up” and accept shared responsibility for a disaster that led to the death or disappearance of more than 6,000 people.

Scientists believe the climate crisis had a role to play in the floods, which were triggered when a melting glacier partially collapsed and set off a deadly landslide and flash flooding through Chinese-controlled Tibet and Nepal in late August. So far, more than 1,300 are confirmed dead and more than 5,500 still missing, with hopes of their survival diminished after 12 days of rescue operations.

events.title: Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flash flood disaster
events.summary:
Chinese man at Trishuli hydropower project and Nepali woman in Nuwakot found 10 days into rescue operation

Emergency responders have rescued a Chinese man and a Nepali woman in two separate operations as authorities continued to search for thousands of people missing 10 days after massive floods hit Nepal.

The Nepali military said on Saturday a joint team comprising personnel from its army and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre (740ft) tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Pictures showed him being evacuated by helicopter after being carried out of the tunnel.

In a move that is likely to set off furious complaints from Nigel Farage’s party, the government will table amendments to legislation going through the House of Lords within weeks that puts the legality of Reform’s latest donations in doubt.

events.summary:
UK general secretaries had been split on issue but sources say they are likely to back strong words calling for action

Trade unions are set to launch an intervention on Tuesday on political donations after the head of Britain’s trade union movement, Paul Nowak, said the government must act to “stop the super-rich corrupting our politics.”

On the heels of the hottest summer ever recorded in the US, the Trump administration has said it will erase any limits on emissions from coal and gas plants that are dangerously heating up our planet.

The US Environmental Protection Agency said it will strip itself of its ability to regulate greenhouse gas emissions coming from power plants under the Clean Air Act, removing a key tool to address the climate crisis.

events.summary:
CDC announces changes to how it reports measles deaths as Pennsylvania continues to confirm more cases

The Trump administration has changed the way it counts measles deaths amid an outbreak in Pennsylvania, which on Sunday saw the third apparent measles-related death in the state reported by a local coroner.

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is now using data from the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), which is a way to track mortality trends over time, according to a note published to the agency’s website on 4 September.

Firefighters made progress toward containing northern California’s Lucas fire, state officials said on Sunday.

Fire officials are still investigating the cause of the fire, which has burned more than 4,120 acres across Lake and Mendocino counties. The fire was 30% contained by Monday morning, according to the California department of forestry and fire protection, or Cal Fire.

Mahmoud Khalil announced on Monday that he’s sued Columbia University, accusing the New York City school he attended of a years-long history of anti-Palestinian discrimination, indifference to harassment, and retaliation.

Khalil, a US green card holder of Palestinian descent, was a graduate student at Columbia’s School of International and Public Affairs (SIPA) when he was arrested at his university apartment by federal immigration agents in March 2025, the first of a number of foreign nationals that the Trump administration has detained and sought to deport over their pro-Palestinian advocacy.

events.title: AfD wants to form a government in Saxony-Anhalt — but how?
events.summary: Following its record election success, the far-right Alternative for Germany aims to form a government. What options does it have without the absolute majority?

events.title: War criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade, Serbia
events.summary: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, has been buried in Belgrade. The funeral, broadcast live on TV, comes just days before President Vucic is expected to call an election.

events.title: Chancellor Merz says AfD result 'changes all of Germany'
events.summary: A visibly shaken but also determined Friedrich Merz spoke in Berlin about the AfD's election victory in Saxony-Anhalt and the CDU's bitter defeat. He insisted on sticking to his reforms.

events.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
events.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, seeking to revive efforts to end the war. But the latest diplomatic push seems to have produced no breakthrough.

events.title: Saxony-Anhalt: Digesting the AfD's landmark election win
events.summary: With well over 40% for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), Saxony-Anhalt has witnessed a landmark election night. DW's reporters were on the ground.

events.title: Fact check: Election fraud claims spread in Saxony-Anhalt
events.summary: False and misleading claims are raising questions about the integrity of the election in Saxony-Anhalt. DW Fact Check takes a closer look.

events.title: Germany set to feel the impact of Saxony-Anhalt's AfD win
events.summary: The state election could have major consequences for Germany's government. Pollsters cite dissatisfaction with Merz as one reason for the CDU's poor showing.

events.title: Saxony-Anhalt election: Why the AfD is so strong
events.summary: The AfD has emerged as the strongest party in Germany's eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt by a wide margin. What is driving support for the far right in this predominantly rural eastern German state?

events.title: Germany, Kosovo unite against ticks carrying deadly virus
events.summary: Germany has high-security labs while Kosovo has Hyalomma ticks and experience with the deadly Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever. Working together, German and Kosovar scientists are fighting the disease and its vectors.

events.title: Germany plans anti-drone shield over Leipzig attack — report
events.summary: Several German cities will receive rapidly deployable units capable of defending against drone strikes on critical infrastructure, according to Bild am Sonntag newspaper.

events.title: Hungary begins hunt for corrupt regime's billions
events.summary: Hungary's new prime minister promised he would recover billions stolen or diverted by the previous administration. A new "super authority" is about to begin that work. Its success or failure will have a big impact.

events.title: Croatia: Toxic waste protest draws tens of thousands
events.summary: The Zagreb demonstrators demanded that the government come up with a plan to clear illegal toxic waste in 20 days. Prime Minister Plenkovic has promised to tackle the issue.

events.title: Germany: From emigration to immigration destination
events.summary: Migration is a sensitive topic in Germany, with public debate dominated by the fear of uncontrolled immigration. But over two centuries, millions of Germans emigrated in search of a better life.

events.title: Germany news: Thousands march at Saxony-Anhalt rallies
events.summary: Ahead of Saxony-Anhalt's state election on Sunday, a democracy festival by civil society groups has been held in Magdeburg. The far-right AfD organized its final campaign rally in the state capital.

events.title: What would an AfD government in Saxony-Anhalt really mean?
events.summary: Detention centers for deportation, mandatory work for asylum-seekers, vigilante groups — the AfD wants to drastically overhaul Saxony-Anhalt. What does the party have planned?

events.title: Outrage as Maltese tycoon acquitted in journalist's murder
events.summary: Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech has been found not guilty of complicity to murder journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Almost nine years after the attack, the question of who ordered her death remains unanswered.

events.title: In Saxony-Anhalt election, small parties will be kingmakers
events.summary: The far-right AfD has good odds of winning an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's parliament this state election, enabling them to govern alone. It all depends on whether other parties make the cut.

events.title: Germany's civil society alliance takes on the far right
events.summary: Trade unions, churches and human rights activists are worried about the rise of the far-right AfD. How can civil society protect people who are threatened by far-right extremism?

events.title: How vulnerable is Germany's infrastructure?
events.summary: The growing number of attacks on substations and railway lines in Germany is raising concern. Experts say that people will have to get used to the likelihood that such incidents will continue.

events.title: The hidden environmental cost of AI data centers
events.summary: As data centers multiply to meet AI demand, they're straining power grids, draining water supplies and reshaping the land and air around them.

events.title: Serbia: How the funeral of Ratko Mladic is dividing a nation
events.summary: As the Serbian government leaves the decision about Ratko Mladic's funeral arrangements to his family, international pressure on the country is mounting. How do Serbs feel about the matter?

events.title: Germany: Is Saxony-Anhalt's economy really struggling?
events.summary: Germany's far-right AfD party has long claimed that the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt has been left behind. Is that really the case? A closer look at the data offers some interesting insights.

events.title: Why North Korea's women's football team is so good
events.summary: North Korea's young footballers enter the U-20 World Cup in Poland as defending champions — the 2024 title was their third. Why is the isolated state so good at the game?

events.title: 2026 Beethoven Festival evokes a sense of home
events.summary: The motto of this year's classical music festival in Bonn is "Home/At Home," featuring musicians from diverse cultures presenting pieces from their homelands.

events.title: How Volkswagen's huge workforce became a costly burden
events.summary: The struggling German carmaker plans to cut up to 100,000 jobs from its 630,000-strong workforce. How did VW's headcount get so bloated, and will the cuts be enough to survive the Chinese EV onslaught?

events.title: Norway seizes Russian ship in Svalbard to compensate Ukraine
events.summary: Authorities in Norway have seized a Russian ship, the Professor Molchanov, on a court order sought and obtained by Naftogaz in Ukraine. Russia has protested the move, which stems from its refusal to pay Naftogaz damages.

events.title: Is Germany's economic slump finally over?
events.summary: Despite a slew of negative headlines, the German economy has posted its best figures in years. There are reasons for optimism, but structural issues remain.

events.title: Macron visits Bayeux Tapestry with King Charles, PM Andy Burnham
events.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is on a shorter-term visit to the UK than the renowned on-loan 11th century tapestry. He viewed the ancient artwork with the UK monarch and relatively new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

events.title: Austria women ice hockey team fight for future generations
events.summary: Austria are getting ready for their first Women's Ice Hockey World Championship. But preparations have been overshadowed by a dispute about conditions, pay and getting men's cast-off kit. A solution now looks in sight.

events.title: EU summons Russian envoy over failed Leipzig drone attack
events.summary: The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the attempted attack had "all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism." She said the EU was summoning a Russian envoy, with France announcing a similar step.

events.title: Women's football: Anyomi, London City and the German exodus
events.summary: Nicole Anyomi has joined Alexia Putellas and other star names in signing for the ambitious English club London City Lionesses. The Germany winger told DW England is a better place to develop her game than back home.

events.title: Ukraine: Russia threatens 'devastating' Baltic response
events.summary: Any escalation in the Baltic region will lead to a significant response, Moscow said.

events.title: Germany says Russia behind attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport
events.summary: Investigators believe an explosives-laden drone was deliberately targeting a Ukrainian cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport in early August. The German government said on Tuesday that it held Russia "responsible."

events.title: Can communities be protected from melting glaciers?
events.summary: Rising temperatures are increasing the risk of floods and avalanches in mountain regions. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet shows the urgent need for solutions, and the tools that could help save lives.

events.title: Can new Apple CEO John Ternus fix the tech giant's AI woes?
events.summary: John Ternus is just the third Apple CEO in 30 years. His primary challenge is to correct the company's faltering AI strategy to preserve its position as a big tech leader.

events.title: At Venice Film Festival, politics take center stage
events.summary: With works about Gaza, Ukraine and Elon Musk, political cinema is in the spotlight at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

events.title: Canada's Carney holds firm against Trump tariffs
events.summary: Canada is facing new US import penalties after Prime Minister Mark Carney refused to match US tariffs on China. Other countries are watching as the Trump trade clash turns into a fight over economic sovereignty.

events.title: Inside the sea cucumber smuggling boom
events.summary: A quiet multimillion‑dollar black market is exploding across the Indian Ocean, driven by one unlikely animal: the sea cucumber.

events.title: Ailing Djokovic 'despised' every moment of US Open defeat
events.summary: Novak Djokovic has exited in the first round of a Grand Slam for the first time in over two decades. Could time — or an unknown health condition — be catching up with the Serbian tennis legend?

events.title: EU wants drones to spray pesticides, but it could backfire
events.summary: The EU wants to lift a decades-old ban on spraying pesticides from the air, allowing drones to be used for greater precision. But experts warn the plan could lead to even more pesticides being used in agriculture.

events.title: This extremely successful author polarizes German readers
events.summary: She's young and she says what she thinks: Caroline Wahl is topping Germany's bestseller lists with her novels. But she has also faced a public backlash.

events.title: What 'The Odyssey' can teach us about climate chaos
events.summary: The Bronze Age collapse may have started with a water crisis. The droughts of today raise the unsettling question of whether it could happen again.

events.title: Influential humanists: These are the winners of the Goethe Medal 2026
events.summary: The prestigious German cultural award recognizes the artistic work and commitment to cultural dialogue of Arvo Pärt, Anita Raja and Prodromos Tsinikoris.

events.title: Germany's military wants to recruit tech-savvy gamers
events.summary: The Bundeswehr has been a fixture at Gamescom, Cologne's video game trade fair, for years. But critics say military recruitment does not belong at an entertainment convention.

events.title: Spain: Thieves steal Bronze Age gold in lightning raid on Villena Museum
events.summary: One of the world's greatest Bronze Age gold collections has been swiped, almost in its entirety, from Villena Museum. A highly professional group of thieves were in and out in four minutes flat before the museum opened.

events.title: Tragedy in Nepal: How do flash floods happen?
events.summary: When flash floods sweep through the Himalayas, there is often little time to react. Scientists are working to understand the risks and improve early warning systems.

events.title: Andre Rankel named Germany's new men's ice hockey coach
events.summary: Germany's men's ice hockey team has appointed a new head coach following a string of dissappointing tournaments. He's two decades younger than the man he's replacing but he has no previous experience as a head coach.

events.title: New study shows German football remains male-dominated
events.summary: The top leagues of German football remain a largely male environment. A new study reveals that only seven clubs have women in upper management levels.

events.title: Venus' US Open invitation raises questions about wild cards
events.summary: Although her current world ranking wouldn't allow it, Venus Williams is set to play singles in the US Open – thanks to a wild card. Who gets these coveted spots—and how?

events.title: The great lake divide: Collapse vs. comeback
events.summary: As some of the world's biggest lakes vanish in real time, others are proving that recovery is still within reach.

events.title: Why social media addiction is so hard to regulate
events.summary: Facebook, Instagram and other social media platforms are accused of deliberately fostering addictive behavior among young users. Yet regulators continue to struggle to rein in their engagement-driven business models.

events.title: Bundesliga season 2026-27: All you need to know
events.summary: From key dates to rising football stars and changes, DW has the latest on the new Bundesliga season.

events.title: Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama dies at 97
events.summary: From works of "self-obliteration" to polka dotted nudes, the pioneering artist developed a unique body of work likely to be relevant for years to come.

events.title: Was the heat of this summer really 'normal?'
events.summary: Some political messaging denies the role of human-caused climate change in this summer's extreme heat. The science tells a different story.

events.title: Tim Curry, of 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show,' dies at 80
events.summary: The gender-bending role as Dr. Frank-N-Furter put Curry on the map in 1975. He then went on to play a number of villainous roles like Gomez Addams, Pennywise and Bill Sikes, but also Mozart and William Shakespeare.

events.title: Reports: UEFA backs off FIFA boycott threat
events.summary: UEFA is reportedly set to withdraw a threat to boycott FIFA tournaments over a plan to partially privatize football tournaments. The Under-20 Women's World Cup is to be hosted by Poland next month.

events.title: Gamescom 2026: What's next for the gaming industry?
events.summary: As Gamescom 2026 opens in Cologne, AI, hardware costs and slowing user growth are putting pressure on the global games industry despite its current strength.

events.title: Remembering Dolly Parton: 8 facts about the icon
events.summary: Dolly Parton, one of the world's most successful artists, has died at the age of 80. Here are some important and extraordinary facts about the country music superstar.

events.title: US country music legend Dolly Parton dies aged 80
events.summary: Representatives of the country music legend told US media that Dolly Parton died after a "brief battle with cancer." Parton's career spans more than half a century and includes a wide array of smash hits.

events.title: Schalke coach looks to Bosnia bond in Bundesliga return
events.summary: After three seasons in the second division, Schalke are back in the Bundesliga. Just a year ago, few would have guessed that their revival would largely be 'Made in Bosnia.'

events.title: Why Germany's Volkswagen could cut 100,000 jobs
events.summary: Europe's biggest automaker, Volkswagen, faces Chinese competition, high costs and US tariffs. What could its restructuring mean for the German car industry?

events.title: Can new US sanctions cripple Iran's shadow economy?
events.summary: The US is expanding sanctions on Iran's financial networks, targeting crypto, gold, aviation and shipping. DW spoke with analysts about what could change.

events.title: Trees are vital for cooler cities, but they need help too
events.summary: Record-breaking heat and drought are putting urban trees at risk. Experts explain how to protect these essential assets and build city forests that can withstand the climate challenges ahead.

events.title: The new Bundesliga season is here, but has the glow gone?
events.summary: Another Bundesliga season arrives, but are the golden years of Germany's top football league already over, and what can it do to change its course?

events.title: Star violinist Anne-Sophie Mutter: 50 years on stage
events.summary: Anne-Sophie Mutter constantly reinvents herself. For her 50th onstage anniversary, the star violinist is surprising audiences with sounds from around the world and never-before-recorded commissions.

events.title: Scientists discover new 'immune hubs' in skull bone marrow
events.summary: "Immune hubs" that actively defend the brain have been discovered in mouse skull marrow. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.

events.title: Spiraling health costs force Iranians to delay care
events.summary: A single chemotherapy session in Iran can cost six times the monthly minimum wage. As drug prices soar and medicine is in short supply, doctors say more patients are delaying or abandoning treatment.

events.title: Sydney Marathon medal wrongly shows German landmark
events.summary: A medal minted for finishers in the Sydney Marathon features a skyline of the city — with one landmark from rather far away. Organizers say the muddle only makes the medal "a little more unique."

events.title: 'Masha and the Bear': Ukraine sanctions Russian cartoon
events.summary: Ukraine has imposed sanctions on the hit Russian children's cartoon "Masha and the Bear," a step towards banning it. The culture minister called the show propaganda. Russia said the move showed Kyiv's "ugly nature."

events.title: Bauhaus Manifesto: Broad alliance promoting artistic freedom
events.summary: Weeks before Saxony-Anhalt's state election, representatives from German cultural, crafts, architecture, design and church sectors unite to promote freedom, openness and creativity.

events.title: Ronaldinho to make football comeback aged 46
events.summary: More than a decade after his last professional appearance, Brazilian superstar Ronaldinho is set for a comeback. The former world player of the year is to play in Italy’s third tier.

events.title: Why Germany's gas storage levels are so low
events.summary: Germany's gas storage facilities are only 50% full as traders bet that wholesale prices will fall if the Iran war ends. With around three months until winter, DW asks whether the country can refill its reserves in time.

events.title: How Europe can better protect against extreme wildfires
events.summary: In another summer of European wildfires that have even seen wetlands burning, scientists say the situation is set to worsen in the future. What's needed is fire prevention and climate protection.

events.title: Bernadette Amani 'living her dream' at Bayern Munich
events.summary: Bernadette Amani is heading into her first full season with Bayern Munich, having joined the club in January. Making a living at football is something she never imagined possible while growing up in rural Ivory Coast.

events.title: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan sentenced to life in prison
events.summary: A Chinese court ordered the former billionaire's assets to be confiscated and fined Evergrande-related companies billions of dollars.

events.title: Who really owns the Caspian Sea?
events.summary: Five countries border the Caspian Sea, but none owns a fixed share. A 2018 convention established rules for navigation, security and fishing while leaving some seabed borders unresolved.

events.title: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water
events.summary: France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.

events.title: Will Germany's drought push up food prices?
events.summary: Germany's main farmers' association has warned of a below-average harvest after drought and crops damaged by extreme heat. DW looks into what lower yields could mean for food prices and grocery bills.

events.title: How to grow food for more people in a hotter world
events.summary: Inside futuristic labs, plants are scanned, stressed and analyzed. The aim is to use the results to produce plant strains that can better serve a growing population in a warming world.

events.title: Do not inhale! How wildfire smoke 'affects the whole body'
events.summary: Wildfires destroy lives and livelihoods. But survivors and firefighters also suffer long-term harm to their health. A growing body of research suggests particulate matter (PM2.5) in wildfire smoke is a major culprit.

events.title: Norway wealth fund sounds alarm on AI stock market bubble
events.summary: The head of Norway's sovereign wealth fund has warned that soaring AI-driven stock valuations could trigger a sharp correction. How exposed is the world's largest sovereign wealth fund to a market downturn?

events.title: Can the cool north handle a surge in climate tourism?
events.summary: With heat records continually being broken and southern summers getting hotter, travelers are heading north. Fragile ecosystems are paying the price.

events.title: Fatty food raises risk of colorectal cancer
events.summary: Did you know fatty foods can increase production of an acid in your gut that promotes tumor growth? That's on top of all the other health risks linked to fatty foods, like fries and burgers.

events.title: US Space Force confirms weapons deployed in space for first time
events.summary: The US Space Force has confirmed for the first time that Washington has weapons deployed in orbit, as the United States, China and Russia expand military capabilities in space. The disclosure highlights a growing focus on controlling the space domain and protecting satellites vital to military communications, surveillance and navigation.

events.title: Bob Mackie, fashion designer for the stars, dies at 87
events.summary: ⁠Hollywood designer ⁠Bob Mackie, ​known for making stars such as Cher and ​Elton John sparkle, died on Monday at 87, according to a post on his official Instagram account. His career ​spanned ‌five decades and included ⁠designing a Barbie doll clothes collection. FRANCE 24's Camille Knight has more.

events.title: Rights group accuses Israel of dismantling 'Palestinian existence' in West Bank
events.summary: Israeli rights group B'Tselem said Monday that Israeli actions in the occupied West Bank form part of a greater project designed to make it impossible for Palestinians to exist together as a people. In a report titled "The Elimination Project", the group alleged five connected Israeli tactics and policies in the West Bank: "violence, ethnic cleansing, movement restrictions, economic strangulation, social and political destruction". FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.

events.title: Yemen: Fact-checking videos claiming to show Houthi rebel attacks
events.summary: A video claiming to show Houthi rebels ambushing Saudi-backed mercenaries has racked up major views on X. But the FRANCE 24 Observers found it is actually footage of 2024 Houthi military drills. The clip was edited with football commentary and blurred flags, which originally show Israel, the UK and US, not Saudi Arabia. Other viral videos falsely linked to Houthi attacks on a Saudi Aramco refinery were also traced to unrelated fires in Texas and Russia. Vedika Bahl fact-checks in Truth or Fake.

events.title: 'The very existence of LGBTQI people is seen as obscene', Turkish activist says
events.summary: Turkish police on Sunday swooped on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ activists, arresting at least 60 people in raids authorities said were aimed at boosting traditional family values, officials and activists said. Turkey's LGBTQ community has frequently been targeted by the government, with President Recep Tayyip Erdogan lashing it as a "deviant movement" of "perverts" responsible for the falling birth rate. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Yildiz Tar, Editor-in-Chief of KaosGL.org.

events.title: Nigeria's Dangote refinery kicks off blockbuster IPO
events.summary: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote launched the biggest-ever share sale on the African continent, listing 4.1 billion shares in his Lagos refinery on the stock exchange.  He framed it as a "people's IPO" to give all Nigerians a chance to share the plant's wealth potentials. Trading is expected to start in November. Meanwhile, global oil prices continued to advance as attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels forced Saudi Arabia to shut down its East-West oil pipeline.

events.title: Nigerian oil refinery Dangote aims to raise 1.6 billion dollars
events.summary: In tonight's edition, Nigeria's Dangote refinery opens itself to public ownership with plans to raise 1.6 billion dollars from retail investors across the continent. Also, President Felix Tshisekedi calls on the National Service to clean up the streets of Kinshasa. And with a month and a half to go until the Youth Olympic Games begin, the Olympic flame begins its tour of Senegal, the tournament's host country.

events.title: Turkey police disperse pro-LGBTQ protesters with tear gas
events.summary: Turkish police fired tear gas at pro-LGBTQ demonstrators in the western city of Izmir on Monday, as activists protested a nationwide crackdown that saw dozens arrested over the weekend in a campaign authorities described as defending traditional family values.

events.title: 'Axis of Iranian centrality' remains "one of more destabilising forces in the region", expert says
events.summary: Yemen's Houthis launched a fresh barrage of missile and drone attacks on Saudi military targets on Monday, as Iran denied any involvement in the country's revived civil war. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, Dr H. A. Hellyer, Senior Fellow in Geopolitics, International Security, and Middle East Studies at the Royal United Services Institute, says that Iran and its non-state proxies "remain to be one of the more destabilising forces in the region alongside the Israeli project of regional paramountcy".

events.title: Leaders urge EU to boost Arctic role to tackle Russia 'threat'
events.summary: Twelve European countries meeting in Finland on Monday urged the European Union to beef up its presence in the Arctic, a geopolitical battleground caught between Russia and US President Donald Trump. FRANCE 24's Eliza Herbert reports.

events.title: Where is the kill switch? AI doomsday warnings trigger calls to regulate
events.summary: Talk about doomsday scrolling. In the past week, our timelines have been alight with dark predictions of our imminent demise, including the one by a Silicon Valley engineer who puts a number on the chances of artificial intelligence wiping out humanity. Better than 10-percent. Triggering the wave of panic, the recent breach of the machine-learning programmers' site Hugging Face by AI machines who banded together to keep their nefarious deeds secret from their human overlords. Can machines actually destroy the planet on their own? In the age of technology, does problem solving always override safety?

events.title: Leaders urge EU to expand Arctic presence amid Russia 'threat'
events.summary: Twelve European countries on Monday called for the European Union to step up its presence in the Arctic, as melting ice opens new maritime routes while growing tensions with Russia and the United States increasingly put the region in the geopolitical spotlight.

events.title: French candidates race to claim the cost-of-living issue ahead of 2027 vote
events.summary: A new Ipsos survey reveals a country gripped by pessimism, with soaring prices the top worry for French voters ahead of the April 2027 presidential election. Candidates from far-right leader Marine Le Pen, to the far-left's Jean-Luc Mélenchon are racing to make the cost of living the defining issue of their campaigns.

events.title: Turkey: Police arrested at least 63 people in anti-LGBT+ crackdown
events.summary:
Turkish authorities on Sunday launched raids on gay bars, nightclubs, LGBTQ association offices and activists' homes in a sweeping crackdown in several cities as part of the government's "My Family is Safe" operations, Turkey's justice minister said.
 
More than 60 people were arrested, according to the state news agency, in raids condemned by human rights groups.

events.title: Poll puts France's Le Pen in lead as presidential campaign kicks off
events.summary: France's far-right veteran candidate Marine Le Pen looks set to lead in the first round of elections next year, as the country's increasingly disillusioned voters seek real change, a poll of more than 13,000 voters has suggested.

events.title: Russian strike on train "terror knocking on EU's door'
events.summary: The Kremlin said on Monday it would keep striking targets across the "whole" of Ukraine, when asked about a rare drone attack on the Polish border that has rattled Warsaw and its European allies. NATO-member Poland said on Sunday that Russia had hit a railway locomotive inside Ukraine, about two kilometres (one mile) from their shared border, just days after Kyiv said it had hit a crossing at its border with Moldova.

events.title: Investors weigh the potential cost of AI 'slowdown'
events.summary: The AI boom that has powered markets and unleashed a flood of investment is showing signs of strain. Calls to slow the development of powerful models fuel doubts over whether the sector's promised profits can justify its staggering costs.

events.title: Countries turn to coal to avoid shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz
events.summary: The US-Israel war on Iran has shaken global energy markets and coal is no exception. Countries around the world are turning to the highly polluting source of power in a bid to avoid shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. According to the International Energy Agency, global coal demand is forecast to rise by ​1.2% this year to a record 8.94 billion ‌tonnes. FRANCE 24’s Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe has the details in this edition.

events.title: Keziah Jones goes symphonic
events.summary: This week arts24 talks to Nigerian Blues Funk Artist Keziah Jones ahead of his Symphonic premier at la Scène Musicale on September 29 as part of Jazz & Musique du Monde season. He tells FRANCE 24's Marjorie Hache about his music and about working with arranger Pierre Bertrand. Plus, we take a look at new releases by Beck, Miley Cyrus and Beabadobee.

events.title: How will EU respond to Russian attack on train near Polish border?
events.summary: The EU's top diplomat said Monday that Russian strikes which hit a Warsaw-bound train near Ukraine's border with Poland shortly after top Western figures passed through were meant to "scare" off Kyiv's backers. "It is clearly meant to scare Western countries from supporting Ukraine, from going to Ukraine to show support," foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said, urging Kyiv's backers to do "the opposite". France 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

events.title: 'What makes China work despite the pain in society?' asks analyst Dan Wang
events.summary: In this edition of Perspective, FRANCE 24’s Stuart Norval speaks to Dan Wang, a China expert whose book ‘Breakneck:  China’s Quest to Engineer the Future’ is a New York Times bestseller. It takes a close look at Chinese life and draws from Wang’s own ten years of living there. Wang says the China and the US are some of the most similar people in the world, as they are both hustlers and take shortcuts.

events.title: French 2027 presidential elections: Why Gen Z has mobilised for Mélenchon
events.summary:
🇫🇷 French far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc #Mélenchon is both highly controversial and a #GenZ favourite.
 
Mélenchon's young supporters express admiration for his promises to stage a "citizen's revolution",  redistrubute wealth, fight #climatechange and support #Palestine. The candidate's critics have accused him of complancency towards #Russia and antisemitism. 
 
Despite being divisive, recent polls predict that Mélenchon will qualify for the second round of #France's 2027 presidential #election, where he would likely face far-right candidate Marine #LePen.
 
So, why has France's Gen Z mobilised for Mélenchon?
 
🔴 FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler spoke to young voters to find out.

events.title: Should the brakes be put on AI?
events.summary: US President Donald Trump says he is worried about America giving China an edge in the Artificial Intelligence market if too many rules and regulations are put on it. In recent days industry insiders, including top executives at Open AI and Anthropic, have once again sounded the alarm, saying that the way AI is being developed could threaten humanity and calling for more checks to be put in place.

events.title: Macklemore 'removed' from Ed Sheeran tour over 'Free Palestine' comment
events.summary: US rapper Macklemore has claimed he's been removed as Ed Sheeran's tour opener after saying "Free Palestine" during a gig.

events.title: Putin ally paid for Trump Jr's wedding celebrations as 'extraordinarily generous gift'
events.summary: Donald Trump Jr and his wife have said a Russian oligarch close to Vladimir Putin paid for two nights of their wedding celebrations as an "extraordinarily generous gift".

events.title: Early results in Swedish election show one-seat advantage for left bloc
events.summary: Preliminary results in Sweden's national election are indicating a narrow one-seat advantage for the left-wing opposition over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's right-wing coalition.

events.title: Uganda back in Invictus Games after withdrawing over 'Harry-Meghan nonsense'
events.summary: Uganda will now be taking part in Prince Harry's Invictus Games next year, after the country pulled out over the "nonsense" related to the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, Sky News understands.

events.title: Six dead and search under way for 129 missing from Indonesian passenger ship
events.summary: At least six people have died and 129 people are still missing after a passenger ship in Indonesia carrying more than 240 people lost contact in the Java Sea during bad weather, officials say.

events.title: Drone alert over Lithuania turns out to be flock of birds - as NATO jet scrambled

events.title: Texas landowners sue Trump administration over border, Big Bend construction
events.summary: The “Conserve Big Bend” coalition says the administration is using its power to build a wall in among the most remote and ecologically significant land with very little border crossings.

events.title: Perez Hilton enters residential treatment program following self-harm incident
events.summary: Five weeks after he engaged in self-harm during a livestream, celebrity blogger and podcaster Perez Hilton has entered a residential treatment program, his family said in an update.

events.title: How Ukraine’s futuristic war could get ‘much worse,’ according to ex-Google CEO
events.summary: Ukraine’s battlefield “kill zones,” where leaving your bunker can mean death by Russian drone within minutes, look set to grow swiftly as the war drives breathtaking technological advancements, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt has warned.

events.title: Man pleads not guilty, denied bond for charges in Tasia Fortune’s murder
events.summary: JACKSON, Miss. — The man arrested in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old Black woman who was found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned Mississippi home last month, was denied bond after pleading not guilty to murder.

events.title: Macklemore says he was dropped from Ed Sheeran tour after Robert Kraft organized boycott
events.summary: Macklemore has been dropped from Ed Sheeran’s tour after he says New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft organized a boycott among stadium owners over the rapper’s remarks in support of Palestinians.

events.title: Fashion council president takes professional leave after grabbing PETA protester at fashion week
events.summary: The CEO and president of the Council of Fashion Designers of America said he will voluntarily take a leave of absence after he was captured on video grabbing an animal rights protester and covering her mouth during a New York Fashion Week runway show Sunday.

events.title: 23-year-old Georgia mayor removed from office after city alleges improper contact with teen, misuse of funds
events.summary: Lawmakers in an Atlanta suburb removed the city’s young mayor, accusing him of misusing a municipal credit card and engaging in inappropriate, sexually explicit communications with a teenager, officials said Sunday.

events.title: Bob Mackie, legendary designer who dressed Cher and Diana Ross, dies at 87
events.summary: Legendary fashion and costume designer Bob Mackie, whose sequined gowns for Cher, Diana Ross, Tina Turner and other stars dazzled red carpets for decades, has sewn his final stitch.

events.title: Trump says AI doesn’t need guardrails, only a ‘high IQ’ president
events.summary: He also alleged the existence of a “sick conspiracy” against AI and data centers, at a time when Americans are increasingly concerned about the technology.

events.title: Ulta’s fall 21 Days of Beauty sale ends this week — these are the best deals to shop before they’re gone
events.summary: Ulta’s 21 Days of Beauty Sale ends this week and features daily deals of 50% off brands like Cecred, Supergoop, Farmacy and more.

events.title: China dismisses AI slowdown calls and blasts ‘fearmongering’ from U.S. tech leaders
events.summary: Urgent calls for a slowdown in the development of artificial intelligence may cite a grave threat to humanity, but China says the warnings are instead aimed at slowing its progress as America’s rival superpower.

events.title: How Ukraine’s futuristic war could get ‘much worse,’ according to ex-Google CEO
events.summary: Ukraine’s battlefield “kill zones,” where leaving your bunker can mean death by Russian drone within minutes, look set to grow swiftly as the war drives breathtaking technological advancements, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt has warned.

events.title: Tracking U.S., state and county gas prices, in maps and charts
events.summary: Are gas prices declining? NBC News is tracking national, state and county prices at the pump.

events.title: Air Force officer recalls ‘free-falling’ after jet was shot down over Iran
events.summary: In an interview with CBS’ “60 Minutes,” one of the two U.S. Air Force officers whose fighter jet was shot down over Iran in April detailed his harrowing ordeal.

events.title: Saudi shutdown of key pipeline limits oil flow as Yemen hits back against Houthis
events.summary: Saudi Arabia has closed a critical oil pipeline after it was struck by drones launched from Iraq, with the latest squeeze reverberating through the region Saturday as attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels threatened to deepen the world’s energy crisis.

events.title: Chinese company releases video of humanoid robot walking off assembly line on its own
events.summary: Chinese company Xpeng released a video showing its new humanoid robot IRON walking off the assembly line on its own. It’s the latest step in the robot arms race between the U.S. and China that could eventually lead to mass production of the humanoids. NBC News’ Priscilla Thompson reports.

events.title: Iran-backed Houthis take control of Red Sea coastline in Yemen
events.summary: The Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have taken control of a strategic Red Sea coastline, further complicating shipping routes in the region. At the same time, strikes inside Saudi Arabia forced the shutdown of a critical oil pipeline, the country’s energy ministry confirmed.

events.title: Rick Springfield opens up about killing a man in Vietnam while performing for troops in 1968
events.summary: Rocker Rick Springfield recalled how, as a teenager, when he performed for U.S. forces in Vietnam, they came under attack and he killed a Viet Cong — haunting him to this day that he “was responsible for the end of a life.” NBC News' Maggie Vespa reports.

events.title: At least five dead, dozens missing after Philippine ferry fire
events.summary: The Philippine coast guard searched for survivors after a ferry carrying 134 people caught fire in the western Palawan province while sailing from Manila. Authorities said at least five people died while dozens of others are missing, adding that 42 people had been rescued.

events.title: 10-year Treasury yield tops 5% as oil surges and diesel hits all-time high
events.summary: The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield topped 5% Monday for the first time since 2023.

events.title: Strikes shut down key Saudi pipeline as Iran-backed Houthis tighten grip on crucial shipping lane
events.summary: Houthi rebels effectively completed a rapid push to take control of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline on Friday, tightening their grip on one of the world’s most important shipping routes and delivering a dramatic boost to their backers in Iran.

events.title: Emma Bonino, leader of abortion and divorce battles that changed Italy, dies at 78
events.summary: Emma Bonino, who rose to political prominence as a leader of campaigns by the Radical Party that legalized abortion and divorce in the 1970s in heavily Roman Catholic Italy, against the objections of the Vatican, has died.

events.title: They led vigils for victims of Tiananmen. Now they’re facing time in prison for it.
events.summary: Three pro-democracy activists in Hong Kong who organized annual vigils for victims of China’s 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown were sentenced Friday under a national security law that critics say has stifled dissent.

events.title: Flight carrying Zelenskyy to Norway was delayed in Moldova because of drone incursion
events.summary: Moldova had closed its airspace to protect planes flying over the country, delaying three departures, including Zelenskyy’s.

events.title: Oil surges past $101 to highest closing level since May as Iran conflict intensifies
events.summary: The price of oil breached the $100 threshold as new flare-ups between the U.S. and Iran stoked fresh concern for global energy markets.

events.title: China hits back at U.S. claim its AI companies systematically copied American models
events.summary: In its most detailed accusation yet, the U.S. government has named six Chinese AI companies that it says copied American companies for their AI secrets.

events.title: Iran attacks American warships and base after U.S. sinks five Iranian tankers
events.summary: They’re the latest tit-for-tat strikes as Washington and Tehran lurch back toward fighting during more than six months of war.

events.title: Widespread flight delays hit major British airports
events.summary: Flights departing from two of London’s Heathrow Airport have been grounded following a “technical issue.”

events.title: Chinese hackers are running AI on stolen networks to avoid detection, Google says
events.summary: One China-linked group targets academic, medical and military AI research, the report says.

events.title: Harry and Meghan ‘surprised’ by king’s letter making clear they’re still nonworking royals
events.summary: A spokesman for the couple told NBC News that a government committee was meeting this week to discuss whether to provide security for the family now that they have moved back to the U.K.
